caption:
Dear Nate White🤍

It’s hard to find words when my heart feels so heavy, but I want to honor you, my dear friend, teammate and brother, for the incredible light you brought into our lives. You left us yesterday, and the world feels quieter without your laughter, your warmth, and your unshakable spirit.

You were more than a teammate you were a brother, a confidant, a spark that made every moment brighter. Your passion, your kindness, and the way you lifted us all up with your infectious energy will never fade from my memory. We shared so many victories, struggles, and quiet moments that I’ll carry with me forever. You had this gift of making everyone around you feel seen, valued, and unstoppable.

Though you’re no longer here, your legacy lives on in every joke we shared, every goal we chased together, and every heartbeat of this team you helped shape. I promise to keep your spirit alive in all we do, to fight harder, love deeper, and live fuller just like you always did.

Rest easy, my brother. You’ll always be with us, in every step, every cheer, every quiet moment of reflection. Until we meet again, thank you for being you.❤️✊🏾

With all my love, 😔
Gideon Ituka

caption:
Day 246. One of the best decisions I ever made💯

I had to tell my parents that I was passing up full scholarships at the D2 level because I believed I was destined for more. I believed in my heart that I was meant to play football at the highest level. I had that dream and I believed in myself so I bet on myself. 

Everyone told me I was never going to be good enough or big enough or whatever but I never listened. Just put my head down and worked. Looking back it was a decision that inspired so much growth in my life. I dedicated myself to a task that seemed near impossible to others but what felt like destiny to me. Safe to say it paid off. Moral of the story - Bet On Yourself🤝

Follow @mason_reiger @mason_reiger @mason_reiger for daily motivation and to support my journey to the NFL.

caption:
The Climb Back.

December 27th, 2023. That was the date of the last football game I played in. 6 Surgeries later, metal rod in my leg, and here we are. On the brink of having it all back. I can’t thank everyone who has helped me along the way, so I’ll thank God. For everything. Every person, every lesson, every setback, every opportunity, every day. 

This season will be an accumulation of the last 17 years of playing football. One last shot, to lay absolutely everything on the line. To make it all worth it. I hope that you all find passion in something like I do football because I really love this game. Tune in this year to watch that passion displayed every game. Go Badgers🦡🔴⚪️

caption:
New summer hires in the spot! First up for team Q&A is @peytonlange2. After a couple years of frequenting the shop and digging around our hip-hop bins, Peyton just got started with us grading & pricing used vinyl downstairs. 

Your house is on fire. There is time to save 3 records. Which ones? 

Tyler, the Creator - Igor
Frank Ocean - Blonde
Nas - Illmatic 

Ask me about: Hip-hop, hard rock, Bob Marley, The Bee Gees, MF DOOM, Johnny Cash and The Beastie Boys

Don’t ask me about: New pop music

Best new music of 2025 (so far): Mac Miller - Balloonerism 

Random fact about me: I have double jointed pinkies so I can bend them in half.

Peyton hails from Minneapolis and plays ball for Bucky. At 6’9” 375 lbs, he is likely the largest indie record shop employee the world has ever seen and has forced us to reconsider all things office furniture ergonomics. Look for Peyton downstairs and occasionally throwing around some vinyl stacks that our aging Dad Bods can barely handle at our Cambridge warehouse location. 

Next up is Caroline, a fellow used vinyl grader/pricer, Madison newbie and @lolasmadison DJ.

caption: Nate the great, skinny back, shifty, all the names we had for you, but the most important is brother❤️I don’t really even know what to say man, this one hurt different twin. I keep hoping you gone call me and tell me that nun of this is real. You was one of the few people I called a true brother. Ever since that night in the hospital I promised yo mom I’d always be there to make sure you was good and I failed her cuh, I failed you💔I should’ve done more while you was here. You was pose to be the one that made it with this football shi. I knew you was special ever since I saw you show up as a freshman in high school. To this day I still don’t know how you could make the whole defense miss and not be touched😂I remember back when we use to talk about how crazy it’d be if we both ended up goin to Madison and we mad it happen. All those hour drives we took coming up on visits, I just wish I could have one more of those even if we wasn’t talking the whole time and you was just knocked out half the drive like you always was. This way too soon but it’s yo time to rest now brudda. I know you gone be with me forever, I promise imma make it for the both of us. The world gone know who Nate White was💯

caption:
Transfer long snapper Andrew Goodman made the trip to Eau Claire Wisconsin to chase perfection!

Andrew and I have been working together for a while now and continue to see progress! Our big focus while he was here was getting his sequence cleaned up so he can create better flow and acceleration while snapping and protecting. 

It’s very easy for most snappers to condense their movement while trying to block. This happens due to them rushing their snap in order for them to block. While protection feels extremely urgent, the more efficient you are, the slower the game gets. 

Andrew made big gains and I’m excited to see where he takes his snapping talents to next!

caption:
TYJ for 2024❤️‍🔥

A year of a thousand endings and a thousand beginnings.

A year of frustrations and learning patience.

A year of new friendships and a love that overcomes the distance.

Like many, the change and progression of college has proven to be some of the most fruitful times in my life. Getting to independently seek out God’s will for me in a new place has shown in a multitude of ways. And in many of those ways, it was full of challenges and tribulations, while navigating this thing called life outside the comfort of my home. Finding peace in the unknown and trusting in the LORD has given me the unwavering strength to embrace the change with open arms. Learning to go slow and be present in the now, creating room for the crushing God has planned in my life, the undeniable power of prayer…the lessons of this year could go on and on. Grateful for the MANY MANY blessing that this year has brought me, along with an abundance of joy! Thank you Jesus for the roller coaster ride of these past 12 months🤟🏼🤟🏼

caption: You can prepare for a moment as much as you want, but when the time actually comes, it’s never easy. This one, especially, I feel like I lost a part of myself when you went to heaven. You taught me how to drive, how to snow ski, how to shoot a BB gun, you taught all the grandkids how to be the best BlackJack and Texas Hold’em players out there, you taught us the importance of how to walk away when you’re winning, the importance of just being practical (your favorite word😌), and most importantly forgetting about materialistic things and remembering the importance of conversations and showing up. You set the best example of hard work and how to give your all into everything that you do. You spent time serving our country and were a true patriot. Most people wait for the day that they can retire, you dreaded the day you had to stop working more than anything. Most importantly you preached putting others before yourself. Every time I saw you the first words out of your mouth were, “How are you?”, “How is school?”, “How is softball?”, even on my last visit. You never were a sentimental person, but in the last couple weeks you said, “I love you” to us more than you did your whole life, but you didn’t have to because we all knew. That’s the best kind of love in my opinion. Towards the end, you said it not because you needed it, but you did it because you knew that we needed it. I’m so proud of how you fought for the whole family for so long and how incredible of a life you lived. You were the glue of our family and you and Grandma had the type of marriage that everyone should strive to have in their life. Knowing that you were content with your life gives me more peace. I could write on about you forever, but I know you would yell at me for continuing to talk about you. I will continue to be strong, I know that’s what you would want. I love you Grandpa, and heaven really did gain the best Angel. Until I get to see you again, RIP.🕊️❤️🙏

caption:
I can truly say this was one of the best weeks of my life @theultimatetrainingcamp. Going into this camp I was hoping to integrate my sport and faith, as well as find a strong community of Christian athletes. This camp did that and so much more. I am so grateful to have met the people I did at this camp and I want to shoutout Team #1, my volleyball team, my small group, Stephen, Riley, and Jackson! You guys are all amazing and I’m blessed to have experienced this camp with everyone there! 

God works in mysterious ways and I’m so grateful He gave me this opportunity to grow in my faith and find a great community. This last year I’ve done a lot of soul-searching and everything that’s happened has led me back to Him. 

2 Corinthians 5:15. He died for all of us so that we could all have eternal life in Him. I no longer live for myself, but I live for Him who has saved me! The Lord taught me this camp that I am loved, I am free, and I am forgiven no matter what happens in my life. If anyone has any questions about this camp don’t hesitate to reach out, I would love to talk about it!

📸 @visualxcarlo

2023 D1 113lb State Champion

It has lead me on a journey full of ups and downs that has taken massive amounts of dedication to get to this point in my wrestling career. I am grateful for all of the support from my family, coaches, friends, and teammates that have helped me accomplish this goal. caption:
Words can’t properly explain a tenth of what this journey has meant. So I’ll just start with the thank you’s. 

To each and every one of my teammates—my chosen sisters and best friends—for making these four years one of the most invaluable experiences of my life,

To Mash a little extra, for living with me for the last year of it, and dealing with all the insanity that comes with that, 

To Kelcy, for putting aside the dumb things I said during our recruiting calls and investing in me anyways, 

To Lexi, for never failing to make me laugh when I was losing my mind, 

To Corrie, for sacrificing so unbelievably much to help me chase my goals, 

To the two of them collectively for always being the best support system in the world back in California, 

To Brenn, for shattering the restraints of my own mind and consistently showing up for me when I needed it most,

To the rest of the Mountaingate crew, for giving me my first tennis family and home,

To UW, for pushing me physically, intellectually, and personally more than I’ve ever been pushed, and for believing in me the whole way through,

To everyone along the way who has offered me grace, patience, friendship, and love, even when I was taking them for granted, 

To the sport that has given me everything I could have possibly asked for and more,

To the game that has touched and witnessed every part of myself with impossible depth, and built me into the person I am today, 

Thank you.

Life’s gonna be weird now. I’m not yet sure who I am without this thing. But I am so grateful that I’ll be able to stay in Madison for a few more years to keep soaking it in. To keep loving this place and this sport and these people who have given and taught me so so much. I hope I can pay it back to you all one day. 

All my love, Forever Forward, On Wisconsin❤️🤍

caption:
i listen to if ‘i could stop the time’ by chelsea cutler for the 27th time today and i’m feeling everything all at once. because i always am. i spend four years practicing to be old and in the end i’m the youngest i’ve ever been. my brain still under developed, more questions than there are answers for. i’m still more heart, less head. and even on my best days i don’t really know very much about anything. which is to say, i might as well be a newborn. and all over again im reminded i’m terrified of all the unfamiliar things. i’m reminded i love madison and for four beautiful years it loved me back. i mean i could never rid every woman i’ve been since i left home. the way i learned to love and hate and love my body all in the same breath. to use my mouth in beautiful and disgusting ways. to practice intentionality. to ask for help. to forgive people i love and to forgive myself. a woman who will always have something to say. i mean one that’s learned to grieve in a way that’s socially acceptable. that will find any reason to spend money. like flowers and coffee and time if i could buy it. which is to say i am growing and it’s out of my hands. as in i’m more simple than i ever thought I could be. i mean i made my whole world between twelve streets. fell in love in all the ways i could and i let so many hearts love me back.i think madison is the only thing i’ve ever let hold my hand on the first try, didn’t even think twice about it. couldn’t even fathom it ever letting go until four days ago. as in, nothing hurts more than an empty apartment. like these four walls held so much love and laughter and agony and everything there is to hold. i mean there’s this dull ache in my stomach or my chest or both and i can’t shake the feeling. that i cannot get this time back. 

i mean this city is underneath my fingernails 
i don’t know how i’m just supposed to leave.

caption:
it’s sexual assault awareness month, a very important month, for me and too many others. and because i love to be vulnerable on the internet, i will be:) 

trigger warning but also surprise. i am the 1 in 4. another girl with her innocence stolen from her. i don’t know how to put a word count on the worst moments of my life. how to encapsulate every scream and unwanted touch into an essay or a monologue or even a book. and i can usually articulate anything but i don’t know how to translate this specific ache into a language i can speak. i know i am healing even if its not as fast and linear as id want. and i am doing all the things. i can engage in therapy and take my meds and drink all the water and laugh with my friends and call my mom and kiss the love of my life and still wish the world would eat me whole. i haven’t told my story yet, because i don’t know how to tell the tale of something that is past yet also somehow present. but i promise i am doing all the things. my love language used to be physical touch and sometimes it still is, but sometimes, it is just saying no and being listened to. i’m still trying to forgive myself for every part of me i didn’t protect, every piece i didn’t fight for, everything i did not become, yet i’m so proud of myself for everything i did.

to survivors:) you are precious. and so far from being alone. i am so proud of you, for being here still. it was not your fault, you did everything you could even if that was nothing. you did your best, your best will always be more than enough. you stayed alive. you are a walking story that you never have to rush to tell. you are also so much more than that story, it will never define you. i believe you. you deserve to be believed. you deserve love. all of it. you deserve to heal in as much time as you need. be kind to yourself, even when it’s hard. even if it’s always hard.

caption:
a girl i didn’t know, died in the worst way. so i cried. and stared at the wall. and fed a hairless cat. and didn’t sleep. and the lights stopped turning on. and my old dorm is now a graveyard. and my daily caramel iced latte with light ice and salted caramel cold foam is cancelled because i’m too sad to go to starbucks ever again. and i picked off all my acrylics and broke off and chomped every last finger nail because i couldn’t be okay if someone died before they even started living. even if i didn’t know them. 

i’m desperately trying to be happy, so here are some things and people i love and pictures i’ve smiled at today. take care of yourselves. there are so many beautiful things that do not fit in your hands, find them, appreciate them, fall deeply in love with them. life is so beautiful. even when it’s not. even when it hurts, even when everything is terrible and icky and gross. there are still so many beautiful things, sometimes you just have to look a little harder for them:) but i promise they’re there. check in on your friends and your almost friends, tell them you love them, give them hugs, don’t take precious moments for granted, please reach out if and when you need help, there are so many people who want to help you. i want to help:) you are never ever ever alone. everything gets better, it really does, and it is so worth the wait.

caption:
My Uncle Lars was one of the funniest, kindest, and most genuine people I’ve ever known. His courage and humor never wavered, even through years of battling cancer. He inspired me through the way he lived and brought joy into every moment he was given. Unfortunately, he passed in 2018.

In his honor, and for everyone impacted by cancer, I’m proud to partner with Exact Sciences, a company dedicated to changing the future of cancer by preventing it, detecting it earlier, and guiding personalized treatment. 

I want to do everything I can to help others in their journey just like Uncle Lars would’ve wanted. This is for him and everyone still courageously fighting ❤️
 #ExactSciencesAthletes #Sponsored

athlete.bio: A fierce competitor with an unwavering spirit, this player's tenacity and strategic mindset elevate the game. Known for her agility and sharp instincts, she thrives under pressure and inspires teammates.

caption:
Les deux dernières saisons ont été particulièrement éprouvantes pour nous.

Nous avons traversé une période marquée par la dépression et l’anorexie mentale, un trouble encore trop tabou dans le monde du sport.
Des choses qu’on ne voit pas toujours, mais qui laissent des traces profondes 

Cette période nous a forcées à faire une longue pause, loin des bassins et de la compétition.
Il a fallu lever le pied, accepter de s’arrêter pour mieux se reconstruire 💪🏼

Depuis mars dernier, nous n’avons pas remis un pied en compétition. Les entraînements n’ont repris que doucement en janvier
Petit à petit, grâce au soutien précieux de notre entourage, nous avons retrouvé des forces mentales et physiques.

La reprise a commencé en douceur. Mais c’est depuis notre arrivée au Wisconsin, en mai, que les choses ont vraiment changé @badgerswimdive 

Les entraînements ont retrouvé du sens, nous avons découvert une équipe soudée, bienveillante, une dynamique qui nous a redonné goût à l’effort.
Depuis, on progresse vite, meme au delà de ce que l’on a pu imaginer 👀

Alors non, nous ne seront pas sur le plot des Championnats de France Élites cette semaine.
On sera là en juillet, pour les Championnats de France Open, avec un objectif simple : prendre un maximum de plaisir 🤩

Bon courage à tous pour ces championnats, particulièrement à @etoiles92natation ⭐️❤️

#swimming #mentalhealth

athlete.name: Lucie Delmas
athlete.bio: A fierce competitor with an unwavering spirit, this player's tenacity and strategic mindset elevate the game. Known for her agility and sharp instincts, she thrives under pressure and inspires teammates.

caption:
After a long period of doubt and questionning, we’re finally gradually regaining our physical and, above all, our mental balance 🧘🏽‍♀️

The sensations in the water are back, the motivation is there, and the desire to perform has never been stronger 😈

This new start, with a team and coaches who are already like family, gives us renewed confidence and happiness 
@badgerswimdive ❤️ @jennahhaney @kabrags @therealmattmartinez @caulibedran @jbrownswim 

Because a happy swimmer is a fast swimmer and we’ve finally found the people and environment that allow us to be fully happy 🤠🍫

Like many athletes, we’ve understood that taking care of your mental health is not a weakness, but the key to moving forward 🧠🎯 

Excited for the future 👀

#badgers #wisconsin #swimming #swim #newstart

caption:
The time In between surgery and fully recovered could easily be a time for me to relax and recover. Especially since I’m not at 100%. But, it also gives me an opportunity…

I’ve always been disgusted with most of my diving unfortunately. Believe it or not it drives me crazy when I don’t point my toes or have beautiful lines. (Despite popular belief). 

Unfortunately, I never took the time to do the small things that mattered when I first started diving. I don’t like to post about shortcomings or imperfections but I think maybe it could help someone going through a similar problem. 

The first thing that I had to do after my knee surgery was work on my health and then my diving. I had to let a lot of my ego go as hard as that is to say and accept that this is my life now. Taking ownership of that was a battle in itself. I could complain and nobody would probably fault me. But to see any results I had to make a change. I have to know that perfection isn’t always going to be there but if I’ve made zero progress towards that then I’m selling myself short. 

In a way this injury is almost blessing in disguise. It’s given me an opportunity to go back and start fresh again with a new mindset. A mindset of gratitude and appreciation for my sport. I get to go back and fix the things that I missed the first time around. 

This dive or any of the videos of diving I’ve taken lately are not perfect by any means but I am a lot happier with what I’ve done here lately. The pressure to succeed through all of this has been an absolute privilege and it has given me a new admiration for my life and diving. 

Thank you all for your incredible support. 

#diving #surgery #surgeryjourney #aclrecovery #gymnastics #injury #springboard #acro

caption:
12 weeks ago I was attacked by a stranger while at the gym. It was devastating to say the least. It was a huge setback considering I was training to compete at spring USA diving nationals. Unfortunately I fractured my femur and tore three ligaments. Honestly at the time I didn’t think I’d ever dive again. Mentally I knew I couldn’t end on those terms. The progress is slow, the pain’s real, and some days just suck. But I’m back on the board, one step at a time. As long as I am breathing there is hope. Thank you to everyone who has taken care of me along this journey.

caption:
It’s MS Awareness Week and I’m proud to be a part of the movement that will someday cure MS! Multiple Sclerosis is a disease in which the immune system eats away at the protective covering of the nerves, causing nerve damage and resulting in communication issues between the brain and the body. 

I’ve signed up for Walk MS this year in honor of my nana, aunt and mom who all have lived with the struggles of MS. I’ve seen effects MS can have on your closest family members and loved ones, and I am raising money for research to FIND THE CURE! 🧡

You can join my efforts by making a donation at the link in my bio!

caption:
In 7th grade my dad brought home some wooden discuses, and my life has never been the same. I cannot explain the joy and encouragement that I have received in this sport from my family, the people in my community, and the amazing people I have been blessed enough to meet across the state and beyond. I am especially thankful to Coach Dave Astrauskas at the University of Wisconsin for giving me this opportunity to become the best I can be at the sport that I love. I’m so excited for the rest of my senior season, and thrilled about the next chapter starting in September.
On Wisconsin! ❤️🤍

Smoked 380/848 and demolished the first American Record of the day, 402.5/887. Failed my only lift of the day of 415/914. I’ve never experienced Amaurosis Fugax, blacking out from the heavy lifting and lack of blood flow. It sucks but I’ll just have to train with that in mind next time

Bench: 3/3
Destroyed 285/630, Demolished the new American record of 295/650, and set the standard for the new American Record of 305/672. Finally joining the 300kg bench club

Deadlift: 3/3
No new records here. Physically just shot and tired from the day. Finished off on a 335/738 pull. 

Total: 1042.5kg/2297lbs American Record 🇺🇸 

Coaching crew: @hartmanperformance @jennica_kingsbury @chloe_lindeman and Jason. These 4 made the meet and this prep possible. They are truly the best in the game 

Equipment: @overkillstrength will still be the brand and the gear i wear. it’s the best and it’s for a reason. If you want to win, stop holding yourself back 

Next stop: Seoul 🇰🇷

athlete.bio: A powerhouse in the throws arena, this athlete combines raw strength with meticulous technique. Hailing from a vibrant community, their determination and sportsmanship shine brightly, inspiring teammates both on and off the field.

caption:
𝐉𝐮𝐬𝐭 𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐞 𝐝𝐨𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐲𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐲 𝐬𝐚𝐢𝐝 𝐈 𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝𝐧’𝐭 🩺👩🏾‍⚕️💅🏾⁣⁣
⁣⁣
I remember my first day on campus, just two months after losing my father, three months after losing my grandma, and five months after losing my uncle. I was anxious to be away from home, nervous to begin my college track career, and overwhelmed by how the world kept moving forward while mine felt like it had paused.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
I initially thought I wanted to be a chemist (I walked into O-Chem and immediately knew that was a mistake, 𝘰𝘰𝘧). But God had other plans. He wanted me to be a nurse. So I switched to nursing and began one of the hardest journeys of my life: balancing a Division I sport while pursuing a nursing degree.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Despite all the challenges, people telling me not to apply to nursing school, days when I ate lunch at the bus stop because I had no time, and running back and forth between classes, clinical, and practice, all while carrying immense grief, I kept going.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
And now, I can finally say—I DID IT!!!! 🥳⁣⁣
⁣⁣
𝐓𝐨 𝐦𝐲 𝐟𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐲:⁣⁣
I love you. You are the greatest gift in my life.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
𝐓𝐨 𝐦𝐲 𝐃𝐚𝐝:⁣⁣
You are my greatest motivation. My life is your legacy.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
𝐓𝐨 𝐦𝐲 𝐟𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐦𝐲 𝐭𝐞𝐚𝐦:⁣⁣
Thank you for letting me vent, for supporting me, and for simply being amazing.⁣⁣
⁣⁣
𝐓𝐨 𝐆𝐨𝐝:⁣⁣
Ephesians 3:20⁣⁣
“May the Lamb receive His reward in me. May the Lamb receive all the glory.”⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Bachelor of Science-Nursing ✅⁣

caption:
There is a photo I look at every day on my fridge, and it never fails to make me cry. 

Before Wisconsin, I was just someone who was lost, looking for their identity. I thought if I tried running and reached out to the coaches, I could find my way onto a team. But I didn’t know what it meant to run for a team. And I really didn’t think I wanted to run for a team, I just wanted to run for myself. 

I pushed myself for myself, not for anyone else. I really couldn’t buy into this “team” thing. 

I dealt with constant injury and I ran because it was the only time I didn’t feel numb to everything else.

There was a point where this numbness crept into my running, and I couldn’t push myself because it felt like there was nothing to push for. And that is when I found myself looking at the women around me. I started believing the things we said in our huddles, and I ran not for myself, but for the women around me. 

So when I was told I had career ending injuries, I didn’t think twice about cross training to get back to the team, or staying six years, or about really anything. Just the women that I had grown to love, the one looking down on us, and showing up for them every day.

I always ran because I loved to run, and told myself I didn’t have to run if I didn’t enjoy it anymore. There are a lot of things I miss when I look back on my college career, amazing times that were had, unspoken truths, and untapped potential. 

But I finally get to run on my own terms, and I am so excited. 

Thank you for everyone who supported my journey and those who I didn’t mention know who they are.

Pressing “RESET” and seeing what I can do.

Before I tried @lagoonsleep I was a restless side sleeper and found myself waking up numerous times during what should have been REM sleep. Since using my perfect-fit pillow, The Meerkat, I have been getting consistent support and have been sleeping deep through the night. I wake up feeling rested and ready to start my day. I have noticed that I feel more recovered going into my workouts and have less of a brain fog in the classroom. Overall I live a more fulfilling life when I get good sleep because I have the energy to do the things I love!

As we get ready to travel for cross country season, I am excited to bring my new favorite recovery tool along with me. So I can get amazing sleep wherever I am!

caption:
That’s a wrap on indoors…

I’ve done some cool things this season! 

I came into college with an indoor mile pr of 5:07. I finished my collegiate indoor eligibility with a 4:38 mile pr and a top 10 mile performance for Wisconsin! One second short of a 30 second improvement in 4 years 😏. 

I made my first big 10 final with some of the best milers in the country! 

I raced in the historic Armory venue in NYC! 

Another top 10 Wisconsin performance in the DMR with my teammates @leane_willemse @emmakkelley @emmakruse_ ! Watch out for us this outdoors 😉

Lots to be proud of when reflecting on how far I’ve come. But competing in arguably the most competitive conferences in the NCAA has me hungry for more.

caption:
Call me bill the way I’m on Capitol Hill!
Last month, I spoke in Washington, D.C. with @voiceinsport on behalf of the Fair Play For Women Act. This bill aims to increase Title IX transparency, education, and reporting requirements to close the gender gap in sports that still persists even 50 years after Title IX was passed. I had the privilege to work alongside some amazing women, and I am so excited for the positive changes we can bring to women athletes nationwide. 
Wisco peeps- check out @voiceinsport.wisc ! #internationalwomensday

caption:
As I write this, with sore legs and a full heart running the Boston Marathon taught me some pretty important things. The first is that the city of Boston during the marathon is unlike any other. From the excitement the city holds to the shared knowledge and appreciation of what every runner did training just to be there whether it be early mornings sometimes before practice or work to late evenings after class or a second practice makes it such a special environment appreciating the work put in.

This experience also taught me that in life you need to stay present and run your own race. Others may fly by you early on, but you may eventually pass them if you trust your training and embrace each moment. Hearing these words personally from @caseyfgilbert prior to the race made those hours on the road so much more special and already looking forward to next year!

Here’s to bigger goals and continuing to push the envelope!

caption:
Humble Beginnings

What started out as a medical diagnosis and what I was told I couldn’t do turned into challenging the limits and asking the question, why not? It turned into breaking barriers, representing the United States internationally, and many goals accomplished and new ones set. 

Recently, what was a thought turned into a goal written on a piece of paper. What was a goal written on a piece of paper turned into a plan. What was a plan turned into action. What was action turned into a result. 

These past few months training in the early mornings and late nights alone allowed for a lot of reflection and growth. Now as I start training for my first Boston Marathon there are some key pieces that have built my foundation moving forward. 

1. Sometimes you can make no mistakes and still lose
2. Don’t give first row opinions to those who paid for nose bleed seats
3. Train like you’ve never won and compete like you have never lost

caption:
@theultimatetrainingcamp was hands down one of the best, and most life changing weeks of my life. I am so grateful to have been bonded with this group of people, and will hold onto this experience forever. God truly showed up in ways I have never seen before, and inspired me to continue growing in my faith. He reminded me that I have purpose, and am loved in a way beyond comprehension, even despite my shortcomings (which happen a LOT). In a world where your athletic performance seems like it defines you, God refutes that with his unconditional love. I discovered a newfound freedom in competing when I began competing for the Lord, and I will carry that freedom with me through the rest of my life. 

My gratitude is beyond words, but I’d like to give a big THANK YOU to my fellow team 3 members. I would not have wanted to do the S.P.E.C.I.A.L with anyone else :) 

We are all worthy
We are all more than other’s opinions of us
We are all loved

Completely humbled and in awe of what God did this past week @theultimatetrainingcamp 

Everything I learned, solidified what is true: the cross changes everything. Only an all loving, all powerful God could gift me a perfect identity that has nothing to do with me or my performances in life or sport. That because of Jesus, I get to access a strength that is not my own and a love and peace beyond description. 

UTC thank you for reminding me of the miracle of the cross and what it means to glorify God through my sport. To everyone I was able to meet and especially to team 12, I love you with all my heart and I can’t wait to hear how God moves in your lives. I am forever strengthened my this community and will carry this experience with me forever.🤍

caption:
LUCIAN LI!!!!
Over the last year, we have seen more rainbows and felt moments of sincere peace among deep waves of grief. There are infinite ways you’ve continued to show up in all of our lives despite your time on this earth being cut far too short. 
A spirit as loving and uniting as yours still finds ways to bring people together and to remind us that you are not really gone, you’re simply waiting for us to join you. I’m grateful for jamming to “hype” remixes, taking the long way home, shopping hauls, protein powder ice cream, rainbow sprinkles, laughing so hard I cried, Gatorade slushies, pep talks, surprise greetings, and endless memes and a lot more. You showed me that time with the people you love is the most valuable gift- even if it meant being 20 minutes late to Angelo’s, and that no detail is too small- like calling to see if I still liked pizza. 
Lucian- my sunshine, my most favorite human in the world, the most fun loving person I have ever met, the best hugger and listener in the world… we miss you everyday but have a greater capacity to love because of what you showed us. The best thing that has happened to me in this lifetime is getting to be your teammate, friend, and finally “special” friend. You make my heart the most happy. I wish I could tell you all this one more time but I know we will all see each other again and it’ll be the best reunion ever. Everything I do, I do it with the power of two🤞

caption:
Game day in Madison! 🏈

We made the trip to watch the Badgers take on Ohio State, and it didn’t disappoint.

This one was special… I coach every long snapper who was on the field today for both teams!

Getting to connect with their families, watch warmups, and see the guys perform on one of college football’s biggest stages was unforgettable.

This season (my offseason) has been filled with opportunities to see athletes I train compete at the highest level. When you stay consistent and chase perfection, great things happen. 

Days like this fuel my passion to keep growing as a coach and to keep helping athletes all over the world chase their dreams. 

If you’re motivated to play at the next level, let’s get to work!

caption:
Day 255. What’s meant to be will be.

These were some of the guys that gave me motivation when I was going through dark times. Them showing me it could be done was something I looked at on these days where I started to doubt. Now that I’m back on the field, I’m so thankful to my old self that decided to keep fighting. Thankful to @nchubb27 @alexsmith_11 _11 @b.robinson_4 

To hear a medical professional say it would be wise for me to medically retire. Retire from the sport I’ve given my all to. It went in one ear and out the other. I knew that God had a different plan for me. I was meant to overcome the odds. To keep fighting. To make it back. And so I did. 

My goal is to spread my story to show anyone that’s going through dark times that there are brighter days ahead. Keep going!!!!!!!!

caption:
My Strength. Their Strength. Together - Every Rep Counts 

On October 12, 2025, I will be attempting as many pull-ups as possible for 24-hours to raise awareness for the International Rett Syndrome Foundation and the Ehlers-Danlos Society. 

I have been training diligently to do as many as I can for months and I feel confident with a little over a month of training left to go. I am so grateful to have the opportunity to raise awareness and funds for these two charities that are near and dear to my heart. I am doing this for them.  I will be completing the challenge at Indoorance Athletic Club (4253 W Betline Hwy, Madison, WI 53711).

Donation goal: $10,000. All donations will be split 50/50 between the Ehlers Danlos Society and International Rhett Syndrome Foundation.

“If all those affected by Ehlers-Danlos and Rett Syndrome can push through everyday pain, I can push through one day to honor them. Every pull-up represents resilience, hope and determination.”

I was beyond excited and fully prepared for this season, but sometimes life takes unexpected turns, and God had a different plan for me. Unfortunately, I’ve suffered another ACL injury, which means I’ll have to step away from the court for a while.

This is not the journey I had envisioned, but I refuse to let it define me. Instead, I see it as another challenge, one that I will face with unwavering determination and resilience. To everyone who has reached out, supported me, and stood by my side, I am truly grateful. Your kindness and encouragement mean the world to me.

I promise to give my all, to push myself beyond my limits, and to come back stronger than ever. This is just a pause, not the end of my story. I’m looking forward to cheer on my Badger girls this season. See you soon better, stronger, and more determined than ever! Go Badgers !! ❤️💪

athlete.name: Nick Levy
athlete.bio: A relentless strategist with an eye for detail, this long snapper blends precision and grit, embodying the spirit of Wisconsin football. Off the field, a thoughtful leader inspiring teammates through unwavering dedication.

caption:
Wisconsin Badger long snapper Nick Levy made the trip to Eau Claire on his bye week to get some work in! Never a bad time to chase perfection!

Nick has been having a solid season but wanted to know what he could do to do even better. The answer, create more flow. 

One thing we noticed after evaluation was that his wrists were staying fairly rigid through the motion which was causing him to lose out on a clean punch through the release. This affects the ball flight in a few ways. A lack of wrist snap can cause the ball to lose speed as well as not travel exactly where you want it to. 

After locking that in, we focused on feeling acceleration through the snap in order to build more centripetal force. When Nick put that into action the result was beautiful. He now has more tools to work his craft and continue to chase perfection!

caption:
Wrestling has been a big part of my life for the last 16 years. I’m a goal oriented person, and the sport has always been my way of competing and challenging myself. It’s more than just a hobby for me. Accepting that I won’t compete again has been difficult, but I’m grateful for everything this sport has given me. I’ve learned a lot about myself, traveled to so many places, and met some of the most impactful people in my life.

I am just beginning a new journey and new goals. I'm not the type to be complacent. I do not know what the new competitive pursuit will be, but I know I have higher expectations for myself than anyone else has for me. I am excited to see where my path takes me.

Thank you, Lord, for the challenges you put me through, and thank you Lord for the strength to overcome them and grow from them.

caption:
For someone who always claimed to be “just a track athlete,” cross country ended up becoming one of the best parts of my life. It gave me moments of deep disappointment and frustration, but it also taught me how to be tough and resilient.

It brought me joy in watching myself and my teammates make progress and work together. I’ll miss the mud, the early mornings, the cold, and even the long runs I swore I hated.

But most of all, I’ll miss stepping on the line next to the most passionate and fierce women I know. I’m so grateful for the lifelong friends this sport has given me and for every person who supported me through it all. I wouldn’t be here without you ❤️❤️❤️

Track still to come — >>>

caption:
All great things must come to an end…
I’m struggling to put into words how grateful I am for everything that college football has given me. There is no greater way that I could have possibly spent these last 5 years of my life. The lessons I’ve learned, the relationships that I have built, and the work ethic that I continue to develop, are all results of the blood sweat and tears that I have put into this game. I want to thank my family for the time, money, support and patience that they have poured into me to help me chase my dreams. I also want to thank all of my teammates and coaches at Tulane and Wisconsin for making every last moment throughout all these years special and formative. I believe that there are no greater lessons in life than the ones that sports can teach you, and I will take that with me until the day that I die. 
I absolutely do not plan for this is the end of my football career, I still have more left in the tank! 
99 Out✌🏼

caption:
Day 316. Just better yourself. 

Sometimes we think the best revenge is in making someone feel the pain they caused us. But the truth is, the real power is in rising above it. The best revenge is living so peacefully that the negativity that once weighed on you becomes meaningless. When you stop chasing revenge and start chasing growth, every step forward becomes you bettering yourself which is all that matters at the end of the day. 

Follow me @mason_reiger for daily motivation and to support my dream of making it to the NFL⚡️

caption:
Day 315. Only the real ones can relate💯 

Most don’t understand the journey you are on and what it takes to be there. The people who say “it must be nice” or “you’re so lucky” don’t really get how challenging this route has been. It’s like anything worth having in life. It takes work. More work than a lot of people are willing to put in. That’s why the successful people find a way to the top. Because they are willing to put unbelievable amounts of time in. It’s a never ending process. Keep going or get left behind. I have to and so do you. See you at the TOP ‼️

caption:
Day 312. Will I get another shot to play? ⬇️

Only time will tell. Hopefully an NFL team realizes that no one is committed to the game of football like me. Hopefully they see what type of player I am and still can be. I hope someone takes a chance on me. The truth is they should because it will be the best decision they could make. I’ve given my all to this game for 17 years and I will continue to do that until the clock strikes 00:00. 

Today is a bittersweet moment because what a great college career but it hurts to see it come to its end. 
Wise person told me “Unfortunately, one chapter has to end for another one to begin.” That’s what today was. The end of a chapter. Excited to see what God has in store for me moving forward!

caption:
What an absolutely unforgettable game. 

My senior night. This was my last home game of my college football career and they don’t get better than this was. A day full of joy, passion, and raw emotion. So many people supporting me doing what I love and because of that, my heart is full.

I have only spent a short time here in Madison playing for Wisconsin but I have absolutely loved every minute of it. I truly believe that God brought me here for a reason and I am so thankful for that. 

The season has been full of ups and downs but I have not let that dictate how much I respect the game of football and the way I carry myself daily. The odds have been stacked against me but to have this opportunity to continue playing at Wisconsin has been nothing short of a miracle. I will forever be a Badger 🦡❤️🏈 One game left. Let’s go.

If you know me well, you know I LOVE making high protein, better-for-you recipes!! I saw this one and had to give it a try! It was a hit. 😮‍💨🙂‍↕️ Just a little piece of what I enjoy off of the pitch. :)

Original video and recipe from @healthienut 

FULL RECIPE BELOW
High Protein Healthier Cornbread
1 ½ cups @Good_Culture 4% Cottage Cheese
¼ cup avocado oil
2 eggs
1 tbsp maple syrup
1 tsp apple cider vinegar
1 cup milk
1 cup all-purpose flour
1 cup cornmeal
1 tsp baking powder
½ tsp baking soda
¼ tsp salt
1 tbsp fresh thyme
1 cup corn
½ cup shredded cheese
Directions
Preheat oven to 375F. Grease an 8x8” baking pan and line with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, whisk together Good Culture Cottage Cheese, avocado oil, eggs, maple syrup, and vinegar until well combined. Whisk in milk.
Fold in flour, cornmeal, baking powder and soda, salt, and thyme until a smooth batter forms. Fold in corn and cheese. Pour batter into prepared baking pan. Bake for 35-40 minutes until a toothpick inserted comes out clean. Cool for 5 minutes before serving.

caption:
Last month, Miss Lily Mae was diagnosed with Ewing’s Sarcoma, a rare and aggressive form of cancer.

Despite the bumpy road ahead, she has her game face on. She wants to be back on her dirt bike, chasing her chickens and running down the road to see if her best friend can play. 

As she goes through intensive treatment at Seattle Children’s Hospital, medical bills, travel and living expenses are quickly piling up. We are reaching out to our community to help financially, so Lily can focus on being Lily and loved. Each donation and prayer will bring Lily one step closer to beating cancer and getting to go home to her family and friends. 

Thank you from the bottom of our hearts for your love, compassion and generosity. And from Lily, “Let’s Go!” ❤️

caption:
I used to measure progress by how hard a new dive was or how many reps I could take at practice. 
-
Lately, I’ve been finding a new love for diving in the basics. the entries, the small details, the things you don’t notice unless you really take the time to care. 
-
Coming back from a knee injury has been way harder than I ever expected, and some days it feels like I’m rebuilding from scratch. But I’m still showing up. Still putting in the work. Still finding ways to get better, even if it barely looks different than before. 
-
The progress has been slow but extremely valuable and rewarding. It makes me even more excited for when I can fully return. One step closer to my full return. 

#diving #entries #springboarddiving #flip #aclrecovery #comeback

caption:
Home from the Pitching Angel Experience with Amanda Scarborough, and MAN is my cup FULL! ✈️ 🩷

160 pitchers from all over the country traveled to Houston TX — all with the desire to get better. Watching these pitchers leave transformed into a stronger, more confident pitcher ready to take over the circle left me feeling fired up and inspired. The growth for these pitchers, even in a short time—was real.

Being in the middle of that kind of environment makes me genuinely excited about where our sport is headed. Watching these 160 pitchers take what they learned and continue to develop, mature, and grow into the pitchers they want to become over the next few years is something I’m grateful to be a small part of.

This experience reinforced how strong the pitching community is and how much more our sport will grow with this next generation of the game. 🥎

To Amanda and Haley and their whole staff THANK YOU x 100000 🩷🩵
